summary: Today’s pulse tracks ​France and Spain race to control wildfires as fresh heatwave hits, as UN warns ‘the climate alarm is blaring’ – Europe live, Trump administration needs to stop ‘public harassment’ of Fauci and scientists, open letter says, and ‘Many people’ trapped inside Japanese shopping centre, others missing in paper factory, after earthquake – live updates. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are before, earthquake, and scientists. In the background, Lindsey Graham’s funeral ceremonies to begin with Netanyahu and Zelenskyy in attendance and Witness says Lincoln Memorial pool was damaged before alleged vandalism keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: ​France and Spain race to control wildfires as fresh heatwave hits, as UN warns ‘the climate alarm is blaring’ – Europe live
headlines.description: Spanish prime minister also says the fires serve as a reminder to plan for the ‘worsening’ climate emergency France and Spain race to contain huge wildfires before fresh heatwave begins Joe Pinner and Jane Clinton Tourists caught up in the wildfires spoke to us about their experiences. “My main memory is how bizarre it was to watch people enjoying holidays on the beach while a major catastrophe was unfolding in full view, not far away. Is this how the world ends?”

headlines.title: Trump administration needs to stop ‘public harassment’ of Fauci and scientists, open letter says
headlines.description: Letter, published before Anthony Fauci will appear before Congress, accuses Republicans of ‘waging a war on individual scientists’ US politics live – latest updates More than 155 scientists, physicians and public health advocates have called for an end to what they describe as the “vilification and harassment of many American scientists” by the Trump administration and its allies. In an open letter published one day before Anthony Fauci, the former top US government science adviser, is scheduled to appear at a high-profile hearing in US Congress, after the Republican-controlled Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee compelled him to testify, the scientists and physicians dismissed allegations against the ex-National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) director as “baseless”.

headlines.title: ‘Many people’ trapped inside Japanese shopping centre, others missing in paper factory, after earthquake – live updates
headlines.description: An ⁠earthquake ​with ⁠a ⁠preliminary magnitude ​of ‌6.8 ‌struck ‌the country’s Kumamoto prefecture Kyushu Electric Power said ​48,000 homes had lost power as a result of the latest ​quake, while railway company JR Kyushu said that it had ​suspended services, including its high-speed bullet trains. Kumamoto airport also shut its runway, as airlines diverted and cancelled flights.

headlines.title: Lindsey Graham’s funeral ceremonies to begin with Netanyahu and Zelenskyy in attendance
headlines.description: Memorials for the Republican senator to start in US Capitol as the Israeli and Ukrainian leaders meet with Trump US politics live – latest updates Two days of funeral ceremonies for Lindsey Graham , the late South Carolina Republican senator, will begin in Washington on Tuesday, with mourners set to include Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Both leaders are also meeting Donald Trump at the White House.

headlines.title: Witness says Lincoln Memorial pool was damaged before alleged vandalism
headlines.description: Former Olympic canoeist Davey Hearn’s lawyers say testimony undermines felony charge A witness in the case against a former Olympic canoeist accused of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool testified that the area of the pool liner was already damaged and would have required repairs regardless of David “Davey” Hearn’s alleged actions. A court filing released on Monday contained that revelation – and in the document, lawyers for Hearn requested access to all grand jury testimony that led to his indictment, pointing to “irregularities” in those proceedings. The Associated Press contributed reporting

headlines.title: Japan earthquake injures 50 and traps ‘many people’ inside shopping mall
headlines.description: Deaths expected as Kumamoto shaken by 6.8-magnitude quake, knocking out power and damaging buildings A 6.8-magnitude earthquake has shaken south Japan, leaving at least 50 people injured. Some are trapped and presumed dead inside a shopping mall. The earthquake hit the Kumamoto prefecture on the southern Kyushu island late on Tuesday afternoon, knocking out power to thousands of homes and damaging roads, bridges and buildings.

headlinePool.title: Banks charged mortgage holders $55m in extra interest after offset account errors, Asic finds
headlinePool.description: Australian banks ‘not getting the basics right’, regulator says after review of more than 200,000 home loans In a new report, the Australian Securities and Investment Commission showed lenders repaid $55m to hundreds of thousands of customers over two years for offset failures, and warned this figure would climb higher as remediation continued.

headlinePool.title: Ex-FCC officials warn agency sending ‘chilling message’ with ABC license review
headlinePool.description: Ex-officials ask FCC to reject petitions to deny renewal of broadcast licenses for eight stations owned by ABC A group of prominent former Federal Communications Commission (FCC) officials, including key staffers and commissioners appointed by both Democratic and Republican presidents, issued a filing Tuesday that warns the agency is trying to send a “chilling message” to broadcasters after it received petitions to deny ABC license renewals for eight of its local television stations. The network’s licenses are up for early renewal after an extremely unusual order from the Brendan Carr-led FCC in late April, following criticism of ABC by Donald Trump and Melania Trump.

headlinePool.title: New evacuation from tourist sites near Bordeaux as France and Spain fight wildfires
headlinePool.description: French authorities order evacuation of almost 4,000 people from Lacanau resort amid return of heatwave Europe live – latest updates The evacuation of nearly 4,000 people from tourist sites on France’s Atlantic coast is under way as the return of winds and extreme heat jeopardised firefighters’ battles to contain wildfires raging to the west of Bordeaux. The precautionary evacuation order, which covers campsites, holiday villages and other tourist accommodation around the resort of Lacanau, exacerbated a wildfire emergency described by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, as the “toughest” situation the country had dealt with “since the second world war”.

headlinePool.title: Mancini reappointed Italy boss after Pirlo controversy
headlinePool.description: Roberto Mancini is appointed Italy manager for a second time - just a day after Andrea Pirlo rules himself out of the running for the job and technical director Paolo Maldini resigns.

headlinePool.title: French Navy carries out 'shooting drill' mid interview
headlinePool.description: Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp says the vessel fired 17 shots as he was giving a BBC interview.

headlinePool.title: AI sell-off intensifies as investors ditch chip stocks
headlinePool.description: Samsung and SK Hynix fall by more than 10% amid renewed fears over AI spending and Chinese competition Business live – latest updates The sell-off in AI stocks has intensified, driving South Korea’s stock market down to its lowest level in three months. Investors continued to ditch chip stocks on Tuesday, amid rising concerns about the huge amount of borrowing among AI companies to fund their datacentre expansion plans.

headlinePool.title: Tories’ Philp rejects French claim that shots fired from naval boat near him were training exercise – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: Shadow minister says there was no warning and ‘it looked and sounded like deliberate intimidation’ Conservative MP accuses French navy of firing shots near him in Channel It is not just the Russians firing on Brits in the English Channel ; Chris Philp , the shadow home secretary, has accused a French warship of firing “warning shots” near him while he was on a boat in the Channel monitoring small boat crossings. In a post on social media , he says: On the channel today monitoring illegal migrant crossings … as I was being interviewed by the BBC just now a French warship approached close and fired 17 live rounds behind us. There was no notice or training exercise in place. Felt like warning shots or attempted intimidation On the crisis in prison places, this has been a long time coming. We did some things, as I said [see 10.11am ], it wasn’t enough, and I’m sorry about that. But I can’t fix the past, but what I can do is come up with solutions for now, and for tomorrow. This was something which we were doing in government. We had plans to rent prison places, just like Sweden has done with Estonia, so that we didn’t have to just release these sorts of violent criminals early. We could have put them in other countries. If everybody says ‘no prison near me’, we won’t get these [prison places] built, so this is something the public can help with … We cannot say ‘no’ to every potential site for a prison.

headlinePool.title: Led By Donkeys wins compensation over seizure of Gaza protest banner
headlinePool.description: Waste firm Veolia pays £27k after ‘Yes It’s A Genocide’ banner taken by Greater London Authority was destroyed The campaign group Led By Donkeys has received £27,000 in compensation after a giant banner it displayed in Parliament Square saying “Yes It’s A Genocide” was seized by Greater London Authority officials and destroyed. Representatives of the GLA arrived on the scene in central London and confiscated the 40-metre by 40-metre banner after it was unfurled on 4 December 2024, just over a year after Israel began its assault on Gaza after the 7 October 2023 attacks by Hamas.

headlinePool.title: As US measles cases rise, biotech firms start developing new treatments
headlinePool.description: The US is making measles great again, so treatment options are needed for the most vulnerable.
